summary: Tested the two reported bug fixes. BUG 1 (Welcome Ride instant-complete) is NOT actually fixed — reproduced 100% of the time, fresh session, cache/localStorage cleared. RCA: the frontend fix (useTelemetry.ts default elapsed 1477->0) only addressed the client-side placeholder shown before the first telemetry frame; it did NOT fix the real root cause, which is server-side: backend/server.py TrainerSim.__init__ still hardcodes `self.elapsed = 1477.0` (line 95). The WS telemetry loop starts streaming samples at ~5Hz immediately on connect, before the client's `sendInit({elapsed:0})` message (sent on 'connected') has round-tripped to the server. So the very first 1-2 telemetry frames the client receives carry elapsed≈1477s, which is >= any workout whose segTotalSec < 1477s (24.6 min) — e.g. Welcome Ride (1200s) — instantly tripping the 'Workout Complete' effect in workout.tsx (completeShownRef locks it so it never recovers even once elapsed corrects to ~0 a moment later, which is why the HUD shows ELAPSED 0:00 behind the already-open 'Workout Complete' modal). Verified this affects ANY catalog/plan workout under ~24.6 minutes, not just ctr-ride-1. Regression-verified a longer workout (Threshold Intervals, 34 min = 2040s > 1477s) starts fine and ticks normally. BUG 2 (Summary screen real data) IS fixed and verified working: header now shows the real workout title + real today's date ('Threshold Intervals • Saturday, 12 September 2026', not the old static 'Threshold Climb'/'Wednesday, 12 May 2025'); Achievements card correctly calls GET /api/rider/achievements and rendered a real unlocked badge ('First Ride') from actual ride history; Recovery card correctly calls GET /api/rider/readiness/today and rendered the rider's REAL prior check-in state ('Do Not Train — Reported chest pain', 0%) instead of the old fixed 78%. One nuance found on the ROUTE/RouteSummaryCard fallback: it is functionally unreachable as coded — rideRecorder.route in src/lib/ride.ts is a non-optional RideRoute that defaults to the same hardcoded 'Alpe d'Huez' object, and workout.tsx ALWAYS overwrites it via setRoute(getVRoute(vRouteId)) for every live workout (even ones ended after a few seconds with 0 telemetry) before /summary is reached — so RouteSummaryCard's `if (!route)` / MetricsGrid's routeName='Manual Entry' honest-empty-state code paths can never actually execute via the only navigation path into /summary (there's no other entry point to /summary in the codebase). Observed behavior is still an improvement over the old bug (shows the real per-workout virtual scenery name, e.g. 'Desert Climb', never the fake always-Alpe-d'Huez text), so no regression, but the specific 'Manual Entry'/'Logged manually' empty states described in the fix are dead code today.

critical.issue: TrainerSim.__init__ still hardcodes self.elapsed = 1477.0. This is the real, unaddressed root cause of Bug 1 (frontend-only elapsed:0 default in useTelemetry.ts was an incomplete fix). Any workout with total duration < ~1477s (24.6 min) will instantly show 'Workout Complete' the moment the WS starts streaming, because the first telemetry frame(s) arrive with elapsed≈1477 before the client's sendInit({elapsed:0}) message reaches the server. Reproduced 100% (3/3 attempts, fresh sessions, storage cleared) on 'Welcome Ride' (ctr-ride-1, 1200s). Fix: change the default to self.elapsed = 0.0 (matching the distance/power fields' intent), or have the server not start streaming/counting elapsed until it receives the client's init message.

minor.issue: Returns available:true from whatever doc is stored under id:'latest' regardless of its 'date' field — i.e. it does not verify the stored check-in's date actually equals today. If a rider checked in yesterday and not today, this will still show yesterday's score/label as 'today's' readiness on the Summary Recovery card (not verified as a live bug in this pass, just a code-review observation of routes/rider.py rider_readiness_today().

ui_bugs.issue: Still instantly shows 'Workout Complete' within 1-2 seconds of starting (ELAPSED HUD shows 0:00 behind the modal). NOT fixed by the frontend-only useTelemetry.ts change. Root cause is backend (see backend_issues.critical). Reproduced consistently 3/3 tries fresh (no cache).

integration_issues.flow: Manual-entry fallback -> RouteSummaryCard / MetricsGrid ROUTE metric honest empty state
integration_issues.issue: The 'Manual Entry' (metrics grid) and 'Logged manually'/'No route was recorded' (RouteSummaryCard) empty states added for Bug 2 are unreachable in practice: src/lib/ride.ts's rideRecorder.route is typed as a non-optional RideRoute defaulting to the same hardcoded {name:'Alpe d'Huez', place:'France', ...} object, and app/workout.tsx ALWAYS calls rideRecorder.setRoute(getVRoute(vRouteId)) for every live workout (even ones ended in a few seconds with zero telemetry) before navigating to /summary — there is no other entry point into /summary in the codebase. So `route` is never falsy and the honest-empty-state branches never render. Practically this means no regression (a real per-workout virtual-scenery name like 'Desert Climb' is always shown instead of a fixed fake route), but the specific UI states described in the fix request were not observed and are dead code as written.

action_items: CRITICAL / primary: fix backend/server.py line 95 `self.elapsed = 1477.0` -> `self.elapsed = 0.0` in TrainerSim.__init__ (or otherwise ensure the WS does not stream a stale/placeholder elapsed value before the client's init message is processed). This is the actual root cause of Bug 1; the previously-applied frontend fix (useTelemetry.ts default) was necessary but not sufficient.

After the backend fix, re-verify: (a) Welcome Ride (ctr-ride-1) runs its full ~20 min without instant-complete, (b) a short (<24.6 min) non-CTR catalog workout also runs fine, (c) longer workouts still behave as before (already confirmed OK).

Optional/low priority: consider making rideRecorder.route nullable (RideRoute | null) with reset() clearing it to null and only setRoute() being called when a genuine virtual route applies, so the already-written 'Manual Entry'/'Logged manually' honest-empty-state UI in RouteSummaryCard/MetricsGrid actually becomes reachable for true no-route manual logs (currently dead code, though not causing any regression today).

Optional/low priority: GET /api/rider/readiness/today should check the stored check-in doc's 'date' field equals today before returning available:true, to avoid showing a stale prior day's check-in as 'today's' readiness.
Optional/low priority: /plan screen has a pre-existing horizontal-overflow / vertical-scroll-stuck layout issue on a 390px mobile viewport, unrelated to this round's bugs.
critical_code_review_comments: The Bug 1 fix is incomplete: the fix description explicitly cites useTelemetry.ts's DEFAULTS.elapsed (client placeholder) as the root cause, but the actual live data source for elapsed while riding is the backend TrainerSim, which independently defaults to the exact same suspicious value (1477.0) and streams it before the client can override it via sendInit. Both places needed the same fix; only one was changed.

workout.tsx's completion effect uses a one-shot ref guard (completeShownRef) with no correction/retry logic — once a spurious high elapsed value trips it, the modal stays up even after telemetry corrects itself moments later (confirmed: HUD showed ELAPSED 0:00 while the 'Workout Complete' modal was already open).

Bug 2's fixes for header/achievements/recovery are correctly wired to real backend data and read well; the ROUTE-related empty-state addition is technically correct code but currently unreachable given rideRecorder's non-optional route with a hardcoded default and workout.tsx unconditionally overwriting it — worth revisiting the data model if the honest empty state is meant to ever be seen.

rca_of_issue: Bug 1: The reported fix changed frontend/src/hooks/useTelemetry.ts's local React state DEFAULTS.elapsed from 1477 to 0 — this only affects what is shown for the few milliseconds before the FIRST websocket telemetry message is processed. However, the actual telemetry stream is produced server-side by backend/server.py's TrainerSim class, whose __init__ independently sets self.elapsed = 1477.0 (with a stale comment '# 00:24:37') and begins broadcasting samples over the WS loop (every 200ms) as soon as the connection is accepted — well before the client's 'init' message (sent from workout.tsx's connectionState-driven effect calling sendInit({elapsed:0, distance:0, watts:...})) has round-tripped back to the server and been applied. Because the WS send loop and the receive loop run concurrently (asyncio tasks), the first 1+ telemetry frames the browser receives still carry the server's elapsed=1477, which is compared directly against segTotalSec (1200 for Welcome Ride) in workout.tsx's one-shot 'Workout Complete' detection effect — tripping it instantly and permanently (via completeShownRef) even though elapsed later self-corrects to a low value once the init message is applied. This explains the exact symptom reported: HUD ELAPSED shows 0:00, but the Workout Complete modal is already open. The one-line fix is to also change backend/server.py's TrainerSim.elapsed default from 1477.0 to 0.0.
